design:
Tier 2 (permission posture, security, a migration).
D1. Allow-all is the existing Full access (`bypassPermissions`); no fifth posture. Resolution: conversation, then agent default, then project default (new), then the runner's posture at rest.
D2. Grants are data, not a posture: Workspace only with no grants is today's Workspace only; with grants it is the middle setting. An agent's grants replace the project's whole, as a checkpoint override does.
D3. The Hub resolves `{temp}`/`{project}` and the agent-or-project choice at trigger time and hands the judge one JSON value in `AW_REACH_GRANTS` (mcp_server.py is stdlib-only; Copilot's in-process judge reads the same variable from the run env). The judge consults grants only where it would refuse a path as outside (`_judge_resolved`) or an address as a network address (`_judge_url`, schemeless host:port).
D4. Codex is out of scope: its sandbox is Codex's own, and Codex is not drivable here.
Hazard: migration 0135 adds three nullable columns (projects.default_permission_mode, projects.reach_grants, agents.reach_grants), no backfill, so every existing project and agent behaves as before; it reaches :8000 on the operator's next restart. Rollback: downgrade drops the three columns; revert the commit. A wider posture is only ever the operator's choice.

problem: On 2026-10-16 :8000 recorded 48 refusals, all from the Workspace judge; about 12 were by design (temp, the project root, localhost) and the operator escalated QA and Architect to Full access to get work done. Posture is per agent only (`Agent.default_permission_mode`, applied at `agent_trigger.py:1195`), so there is no project-wide setting. A Copilot spec turn under Full access is judged as Workspace (`copilot_acp._decide_permission`, `judged = WORKSPACE if spec_turn and posture == _FULL`). Between Workspace only and Full access there is nothing: the judge (`mcp_server._judge_resolved`, `_judge_url`) refuses every path outside the workspace and every address but the run's own Hub.

requirements.statement: The capability MUST say that the workspace boundary is a guardrail against an agent's mistakes, not containment: the judge reads what a call says, not what the process does.

requirements.rationale: reach-D2: settable for every agent in a project or for specific agents.
requirements.statement: A project MUST have a default posture, `default_permission_mode` on PUT /projects/{id}/settings (a catalog posture or null), that a run of any of its agents receives when neither the conversation nor the agent states one; the agent's own default MUST win over it in either direction, and the agent roster's at-rest posture MUST report it.
Full access MUST be offered and honoured for a Copilot agent, set on the agent or the project: the run asks Copilot for allow-all, and the Hub allows whatever Copilot still asks.

A Copilot specification turn under Full access MUST have its requests other than edits allowed, not judged as Workspace only; it still writes no file and keeps its runner's widening flags stripped (the F4 role boundary, not reach).

requirements.rationale: reach-D3: the middle setting, project level with a per-agent override. A shell word cannot say whether it reads or writes, so a shell command needs a readwrite root.
requirements.statement: A project MUST hold reach grants (`reach_grants`: roots, each `read` or `readwrite`, an absolute path or `{temp}` / `{project}`; hosts as `host`, `host:port`, `host:*` or `*.domain`), and an agent MAY hold its own, which replaces the project's whole (null inherits). Wherever the workspace judge decides for a Claude or Copilot run, a path inside a readwrite root MUST be allowed, a path inside a read root only for a read tool (Read, Glob, Grep, LS, Copilot read), and a shell address whose host a grant names MUST be allowed; every other outside path and address MUST be refused as today.

requirements.rationale: reach-4, the recommendation: keep the record, out of the way.
requirements.statement: Under every posture, Full access and granted roots included, a write outside the workspace MUST still be recorded on the run, and the run's row in the conversation MUST show it, with no card.

summary: The operator can give agents more room (reach-1019): a project-wide default posture with a per-agent override either way, Full access (allow-all) that really covers Copilot and spec turns, and a middle setting, Workspace only plus granted roots and hosts. The boundary is a guardrail against an agent's mistakes, not containment, and writes outside the workspace stay recorded on the run under every posture.
